_luxury_note: DVW-B3-LUX (owner 2026-10-23, 'luxury imports, costly caravan goods (spices, fine cloth, jewellery) bought for status, the coins leaving with the caravan'): the market town Wulstead and the rich abbey town Higham-on-the-Way hold luxuries in their traders' stock from the start (GAME EXPANSION and provisional; lore basis BTWO-C14-P002, the chapman's booth of 'fine cloth plumbed with the seal of the greatest of the cities; and silk of Babylon, and spices of the hot burning islands, and wonders of the silversmith's and the goldsmith's fashioning', and BONE-C3-P031, Higham's 'no better market betwixt this and Babylon'). They come from beyond the map, are part of the settlement's opening books like any stock and are not made, restocked or wanted by the settlement: what the village buys leaves the trader's stock for good, its coins stay in the trader's till.
_materials_note: B25 Decision 5 (owner 2026-11-01): the materials of the production economy are made in the region too, within the settlements' books: Garton's diggings hold a finite tin reserve (quarry tin_ore, reserves), every forge smelts tin, alloys bronze (copper and tin) and makes steel (iron and coal) by the village's own recipes, every tannery dresses some hides as fur, and the weavers keep silkworms (abstract production, out silk, GAME EXPANSION: no mulberry or silkworm is simulated) and weave raw silk into fine cloth. Higham's trader also holds raw silk from beyond the map at the start. The traders carry tin ore and raw silk to the village (carry). A save made before this gains the new outputs and reserves on load (OffMapSettlement.add_new_outputs), nothing else. Agent proposals, provisional (docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-11-01).
_note: Expansion 18 SET-C-SIM / SET-C-FIVE (owner 2026-10-23, Q18-3, Q18-4, ECON-P1.3): the five off-map settlements, each a simulated economy 'just like this one' at lighter detail (real households with members, purses and pantries; a manor or council treasury; businesses with their own tills, stocks and workers), stepped once a day by Regions/OffMapSettlement without walking anyone. The PLACES are lore (docs/world/B_GAZETTEER.md; docs/expansion18/SETTLEMENTS.md cites paragraph ids and labels each claim); the trades, deposits, sizes and every number below are GAME EXPANSION and agent proposals (provisional). Money enters a settlement only through trade with the village or another settlement and leaves the same way; nothing is created.

trade._note: REGION-NAV-01 S6 (agent proposal, provisional): villagers trading with the neighbouring places on what they were told (RegionTrade). per_day: tradespeople who weigh their records each dawn; day_value: the coins a day on the road is worth to them; min_gain: the least gain worth a trip; buy_max: the most they set out to buy; regional_days: a founding counts as regional when its trade sent goods to a neighbour within this many days (S7).

seed_travelers._note: B25R1-009 (owner 2026-11-03, seed travelers; numbers an agent proposal, provisional): at the founding of a new world, count village residents set out to buy one ordinary item (price at most max_price, paid from their own coins above their reserve) from a merchant of another settlement and walk home with it (SeedTravelers). wait_mornings: mornings a seed traveller waits at the site for a seller away on the caravan road before going home with nothing. skip_jobs: posts the village cannot spare (never chosen). Only at the founding: never on loading, never again.

intel._note: REGION-NAV-01 S5 (agent proposal, provisional): what villagers know of the neighbouring places' trade (Intel). stale_days: a record older than this (from the day it was collected) is not acted on; forget_days: a villager forgets it; keep: records a villager holds (freshest kept); share_max: records told in one shared hour; tell_max: tradespeople the envoy tells a mission; tell_minutes: one telling.

envoy._note: REGION-NAV-01 S4 (agent proposal, provisional): the reeve's envoy post. day_wage: the manor's coins a day of the trip (2 x route days + 1), set aside when taken; refresh_days: a settlement surveyed this long ago is surveyed again; talk_minutes: an interview; survey_minutes: the home survey at the manor; spare_days: days beyond the trip before an unfinished mission lapses.

independent._note: REGION-NAV-01 Q4 (owner 2026-11-03, option C: independent crafting and self-employment within the regional economy): per settlement, the households working on their own account at the start (OffMapSettlement._setup_own): a new household of the trade with `capital` coins in its working purse; an independent miner digs a claim of its own (`out` a day, `reserves` finite), never the quarry business's. Others set up on their own as the weeks go by (OffMapSettlement._own_week: one a week, a craft household earning under switch_below with own_start_capital saved) and go back to their trade's business after own_fail_days days with the working purse spent. PROVISIONAL agent values.

site._note: REGION-NAV-01 AD-1 (owner 2026-11-02, Build 25 scope): each settlement stands in the overworld as a site centred on its position (x tiles across, miles x tiles_per_mile south of the village's centre: the geography the regional trade measures distances by), joined to the road network; overworld GEN_VERSION 3. Its trades (in this file's order) each have a building, a village building stamp, in rows of `cols` with `gap` tiles between them and a `lane` under each row onto which the doors open; `margin` round the whole. `stamps`: trade -> stamp (others: house). Agent values.

rules._note: Prices float with yesterday's imbalance inside the village's own price band (balance.json price_min and price_max). Food, tax and wage rules follow the village's (balance.json hunger_per_hour, child_food_factor, tax_rate_*, tax_exemption_*, treasury_reserve_days).
rules._food_trade_note: X20-SETTLE-FOOD (owner REG-BUY-D1, 2026-10-23; agent engineering, provisional, docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-10-30): on the traders' wholesale day a settlement short of food (under three days for its people, counting food on the road) sends its trader to buy these foods from another settlement's trader, through RegionalMarket at the seller's own price; the goods arrive after the trip there and back. Wheat is the staple every place grows and the unit the traders reckon a food shortfall in.
